alignments.note: The iterative conjunction is realized by every, the word by which the ASV writes the whenever sense; its own gloss note records the Greek as whenever evening came.

The ASV compresses whenever evening came into every evening and writes no word for the verb of becoming; nothing is left for it, so rule 23 makes it its own unit. Stretching every over ὅταν and ἐγένετο as one unit remains defensible; a reference comparison reporting this token is not a correction.

The compound verb of the selected reading r01 keeps its supplied subject and the particle forth realizing its preverb under rule 106; the following ἔξω has its own English word, so forth is not that preposition's.

Improper preposition governing a genitive; the ASV writes a determiner for the governed noun, so under rules 42 and 101 the article takes it along with the case preposition and the adverb stands bare on out.
Article with its case preposition riding under rule 21, headed on the.

review_notes: ἐγένετο left unrepresented because the ASV's every evening writes no word for it; the note records the competing joint reading.
ἔξω τῆς πόλεως split as in rule 42's πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης: out to the adverb, of the to the article.
